title: Web Design Riyadh: Arabic-First Websites | The Brandle
description: Web design for Riyadh and Saudi Arabia. Arabic-first websites and stores with Mada, Apple Pay and Tamara at checkout and 15% Saudi VAT handled.

hub.name: Web design Riyadh
hub.line: Arabic first. English is the translation.

hero.joke: Arabic isn't English flipped in a mirror. We've seen the websites that thought it was.
hero.intro: Web design for Riyadh and the wider Saudi market, from a studio in Dubai. Arabic-first websites and online stores, with the payment methods Saudi shoppers use and 15% VAT handled correctly.

items.p: Right-to-left is the main direction, designed first. English is the translation, not the other way round.
Mada, Apple Pay, STC Pay and Tamara instalments, connected through a gateway that supports them.
15% Saudi VAT displayed and invoiced properly, with the fields your accountant will ask for.
Hosting chosen for quick loading in Saudi Arabia. If your data has to stay in the Kingdom, tell us at the start and we plan around it.
Page titles, descriptions and addresses written for how people search in Arabic, not translated from the English ones.
Designed for phones before desktops, and tested on them.

fit.p: A site built for another market and translated into Arabic reads like exactly that. If Saudi Arabia is a serious part of the plan, the Arabic version is the real website and the English one is the extra.
yes: A Saudi business that needs an Arabic-first site
A Gulf brand expanding into the Kingdom
Selling online and in need of Mada and Saudi VAT
Stuck with a site that was designed for somewhere else
fit.no: Arabic is a nice-to-have for you. Then a bilingual build from [web design Dubai](/services/web-design-dubai/) is enough. If checkout is the only issue, go to [payment gateway integration](/services/payment-gateway-integration/).

items.p: A free video call. Riyadh is an hour behind Dubai, so mornings work for everyone. A fixed quote follows.
Key pages designed in Arabic first, with real Arabic copy, not placeholder text.
Both languages built and payments connected in test mode. Our working weeks overlap from Monday to Thursday, which is plenty.
Real test payments, VAT checked on real invoices, then live. Free fixes for 30 days.

price.p: Our fixed plans run from $1,299 to $6,499, and a site or store takes 3 to 6 weeks. Two languages and Saudi payment set-up add scope, which the quote will show. Translation is separate, and we can recommend translators.

tools.note: Payment methods we can connect through a gateway that supports them. Mostly written as words, because that's how their owners prefer it.

faq.a: Yes. Right-to-left is the primary layout, with Arabic type chosen for reading on screens. Our [Arabic and RTL guide](/blog/arabic-rtl-website-design/) shows what changes.

faq.q: Which payment methods matter in Saudi Arabia?
faq.a: Mada is the domestic card network, so it comes first. Then Apple Pay, STC Pay and Tamara for instalments. We set up whichever your gateway and licence allow.

faq.q: Can you work with us from the UAE?
faq.a: Yes. Riyadh is one hour behind Dubai. The Saudi week runs Sunday to Thursday and ours runs Monday to Friday, so four working days overlap. We reply within one business day.

faq.q: Do you provide the Arabic copy?
faq.a: We design for it and can recommend translators. Native copywriting is a specialist's job, and we won't run your brand through a translation tool and hope.

post.title: Arabic and RTL website design: doing it properly

cta.p: Tell us about the business and who you're selling to. We reply within one business day.
